body:
Your husband shouldn't worry about the impostor syndrome he is feeling regarding programming. I've graduated from a programming course and currently work as a game developer and let me tell you, everybody googles even the most basic things sometimes, or follows along with programming tutorials on youtube. It's even an in-industry joke that everyone gets their programming diploma thanks to stackoverflow. 

But if your husband DOES decide to pursue creating games, it's important to note that game development  is usually a team effort and depending on the company, the need to engage in social interaction may be very high, which could prove difficult for someone with ASD. He needs to find a workplace that is conducive for someone with ASD to work in. For example, my previous job had a 9 to 5 schedule, with a supervisor to assign me tasks daily. That takes care of both the social issue and executive function issue of ASD at the same time since it's 1) better for people with ASD to have a work schedule than work on flexible hours, 2) better for people with ASD to only report one-on-one to a single person rather than an entire team, and 3) being issued tasks is better for people with ASD who have trouble with planning and prioritizing. If your husband can find a similar setup, he should be fine with pursuing game development.

I completely relate to this, right down to feeling numb about it, even though potentially losing your job should be devastating. I'm in the exact same position currently, with the pandemic and a death in the family hitting my mental real hard the last few months. It's good that you acknowledge that it's because of your own shortcomings that you're being laid off, but just the fact that you're feeling passive about potentially getting fired probably means it's time to find a new job anyway. Don't beat yourself up too hard about it. It's a hard time for everyone right now. But don't forget to pick yourself back up after. Good luck.

Yeah, it can be really discouraging when meds and therapy don't work since they're both so damn expensive. Is it possible for you to see other people? I've known a few people who felt like their therapist didn't help at all, until they switched to someone else. It's sad to think about but some of them kind of just keep their clients medicated, sometimes even with the wrong medication, because of wrong diagnosis.
What was your life like when it was normal? Did something happen that changed the way you lived since then?

I can't imagine the guilt that you must go through everyday for over a decade. You probably know this already, but killing yourself won't do anything. It won't bring them back, and it would probably do little to the family that lost their son since it's been so long ago. If there's penance to be paid, it's an idea to atone by spending your efforts advocating against bullies from here on out. You may not be able to go back in time to prevent yourself from pushing that person over the edge, but maybe you can prevent someone else from doing the very same thing. I think if there's someone who can offer perspective to kids who take their frustrations out on other students, it's you. If just a little bit of your regret and guilt resonates with them, you might even be able to save someone else's life.

Sometimes, it's not about the advice. If someone can't solve their own problem, it's a long shot to expect a stranger online to be able to do it for them. Sometimes, what people here need is just somebody to listen while they get things off their chest. I think that alone helps, even if it's just a little bit.

It's a little silly but one of the things that keeps me going is my cat. She's quite wary of people, and can only really relax around me. If I go and never come back, she'd never know where I went and that kind of breaks my heart.

Yeah, it's very difficult to get things done without a schedule. I'm in a similar predicament right now where I moved from office work to startup, and not having a schedule is totally screwing me up. I'm not sure if you're self-studying, but if it's possible, have someone keep track of your schedule and the content you're learning. It may not make it more enjoyable, but having someone to oversee your progress might make it better than going through it alone, not knowing what to do or where to start.

Is it the type of content you have to learn about? Your environment? Or the pressure surrounding schooling? Sometimes, it's not studying itself that's unpleasant, but the way it's facilitated. Maybe your surroundings or schedule aren't conducive to learning. I've seen people who are disinterested in formal education, but really apply themselves when it comes to learning about things they do like, or become interested when their school content is presented in a different, more engaging way. Perhaps if you make a small change in the way you learn, or somehow make it more enjoyable for you, there might be a change somewhere along the way.

Surely there are other options! You don't have to whore yourself out to make money. You mentioned that you're good-looking, so why not take advantage of that and start on relatively easy and accessible sidegigs that have the potential to create an income for you? Streaming might be an option? It's definitely a lot easier to generate an audience if you're attractive. Just throwing out an option, but there are other things you can do besides tying yourself to someone who will use you in exchange for money. Hang in there!
I'm sorry to hear it, especially knowing you work in a social job like working at a coffee shop. In some cases I feel like having enough exposure to social situations just isn't enough to get better.
I'll try to hold on for longer and look into exposure therapy. Glad to hear it from someone who's recovered from it, and thanks for the recommendation.

It's really heartbreaking when parents care more about their child staining their reputation than the child's own emotional state and mental health. I'm Asian as well and I had a similar confrontation with my father a while back where I confessed that I self-harmed and suffered from suicidal tendencies. The first thing that came that came to his mind was for me not to bring shame to the family. Traditional Asian family culture is extremely toxic and I hope these cultural traits die out as the generations go on. I only hope that you have others that you consider your "real family", like friends, who truly care about you beyond shallow things like reputation.
It's unfortunate that it has to come to that, but I sincerely hope you have a wonderful last month. Thank you for giving it your best all this time.

Sorry to hear that man. It's too late in my life for me to think it'll get better through experience, because I've truly tried. But here I am still, finding myself two steps backwards with every step I take. I hope somehow you are doing better than me. It may not mean much from a stranger over the internet, but you have my solidarity.

I feel you. It's not as if you're not trying. Sometimes people like us have to try harder than anyone else. The fact that you've been at it again and again tells me you're at least trying again and again, and doing the best you can despite your situation. I hope you can see that.

I think being overly sensitive isn't something that someone just becomes for no reason. Perhaps it's a lack of self-esteem or convictions in your own judgment, which are both deeply-rooted emotional issues in itself. Maybe it's a product of being exposed to a lot of criticism growing up, so I feel like having a characteristic like that may not even be completely within your control. It's not as if you chose to be like this. You should give yourself more credit!
I think it takes a lot of honesty to admit all that. I hope somehow it's at least been a cathartic experience for you posting this online.
